summary: Born into poverty in Czechoslovak Ruthenia in 1923, Robert Maxwell fought the Nazis and committed war crimes, then built Pergamon Press into a profit machine for scientific publishing and looted his employees' pension fund before dying at sea in 1991.

evidence.note: born June 1923 in a Ruthenian village then in Czechoslovakia, now in Ukraine
1939 Nazi takeover; he leaves the yeshiva to join the anti-Nazi underground
after learning his family died at Auschwitz he kills prisoners and a German mayor
joins Czech unit in France, evacuated at Dunkirk, later fights from Normandy into Germany
spy work for British intelligence in occupied Berlin; MI6 alleged to fund his startup
takes control of the Butterworth-Springer venture in 1951 and names it Pergamon Press
exclusive author contracts and endless new journals sold to libraries at huge margins
extended look at how the for-profit journal model he built works today
1969 Steinberg deal exposes inflated accounts; 1971 inquiry finds him unfit to run a company
uses the Mirror to campaign against union leader Arthur Scargill
mid-1980s heavy investment in Israel and passing information to Mossad
raids the pension fund, then dies falling from his yacht off Tenerife in November 1991

notes: main_span starts at his 1939 entry into the anti-Nazi underground because the whole first part is his war service and war crimes; a strict encyclopedia reading would start at Pergamon in 1951. Primary theme chosen as corporate-malfeasance (journal pricing racket, pension raid); fraud-grift is a close alternative. Brief political career (Labour MP 1964-70) not given its own theme.
